title: AWS Introduces Foreign Key Constraints in Aurora DSQL
gist: AWS added foreign key constraints to Aurora DSQL, closing what users called the biggest gap versus standard Postgres and a key blocker for brownfield migrations. Enforcement uses snapshot checks plus commit-time KEY SHARE conflict detection, so conflicts cause transaction failures (requiring retries) and extra reads that AWS says to benchmark.

insights.claim: Aurora DSQL now supports foreign key constraints including CASCADE and SET NULL, addressing a gap users explicitly called an adoption blocker.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Removes a key barrier to AWS's distributed SQL product winning Postgres workloads.
insights.quote: The addition addresses a long-standing gap that users had explicitly called out as an adoption blocker.

insights.claim: Luc van Donkersgoed said lack of foreign keys was the biggest gap between DSQL and normal Postgres and blocked many migrations, so the change makes DSQL much more viable for brownfield environments.
insights.speaker: Luc van Donkersgoed
insights.so_what: Opens the larger brownfield migration market to DSQL, expanding AWS database TAM.

insights.claim: DSQL enforces referential integrity via snapshot verification during transactions and implicit KEY SHARE checks at commit, without table locks; violating transactions are rejected with a serialization error.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Optimistic design preserves scale but shifts conflict handling onto applications.

insights.claim: Marc Brooker claims the design has no blocking, no change in scaling for non-FK reads, and great FK scaling for well-distributed workloads.
insights.speaker: Marc Brooker
insights.so_what: Vendor claim that the feature does not compromise DSQL's scaling pitch.
insights.quote: No blocking, no change in scaling for non-FKC reads, FKC readers never cause other readers to abort, and great FKC scaling for well-distributed workloads.

insights.claim: Because concurrent conflicts cause failures rather than waits, applications need retry logic, and AWS advises keeping heavily referenced keys stable and moving changing values to non-key columns.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Migration cost is not zero: apps must be adapted for optimistic concurrency.

insights.claim: A Reddit user warned foreign keys slow things down a lot and questioned how well they fit DSQL's architecture; AWS itself notes all DML on referencing tables incurs additional reads and advises benchmarking first.
